clue.text: Accessories worn with kind of shirt — striking on first sight

indicators.note: the first letter of 'sight' is the one taken

blocks.note: a T-shirt is a kind of shirt

explanation.surface: A fashion note about accessories chosen to catch the eye with a particular shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of shirt' is just its letter: T, as in T-shirt. 'Striking on first sight' reads as eye-catching, but splits into RAPPING followed by S.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the accessories and outward adornments that go with something.

clue.text: Experimental equipment for examination underground

blocks.note: the Tube is the London Underground

explanation.surface: Kit for examining something below ground, perhaps a geological survey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; the surface wants 'underground' to describe where the examination happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is basic laboratory equipment for experiments.

clue.text: Unfriendly, when a clown shows up

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a fool is a clown; it turns upward to LOOF

explanation.surface: Someone turns cold the moment a clown appears at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows up' pretends to mean arrives, but in a down entry it sends the clown upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and cool towards others, i.e. unfriendly.

clue.text: Finding gift that's absolutely right makes one tense

explanation.surface: The strain of hunting for exactly the right gift leaves someone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' pretends to mean anxious; it is the grammar term, and the present perfect ('I have given') is one tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the grammar form built from 'have' plus a past participle, as in 'I have found'.

clue.text: Freshly made hot flan gets an enthusiastic response

indicators.note: the letters are made up afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A flan straight from the oven is greeted with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'yes, very much', so despite its words it is an eager yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked 'Do you want some?', 'Not half!' means 'absolutely', an enthusiastic reply.

clue.text: What's used to sweeten pudding courses when processed

indicators.note: processing turns the letters into something new

explanation.surface: A question about what goes into a dessert course during preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pudding courses' reads as one phrase, but the break comes after 'pudding': the definition ends there and COURSES is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is ordinary table sugar, used to sweeten puddings.

clue.text: The whole team made the cut

blocks.note: everyone working a boat or a film set together
read not as 'got selected' but as the word that turns 'cut' into a short military haircut

explanation.surface: Every player was picked for the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a hairstyle: a crew cut, so 'crew' makes the cut into a haircut. 'Made the cut' pretends to mean selected, as the whole team was.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a whole team working together, as on a boat or film set.

clue.text: Shape emerges from half-hidden recess leading to confusion

indicators.note: half the word is hidden away, leaving the other half

blocks.note: RECESS with its second half (ESS) hidden

explanation.surface: A form slowly takes shape out of a shadowy alcove, causing bewilderment.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of 'recess' shows, and it leads straight into the confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided shape with right angles.

clue.text: Showing no restraint, boy grabs daughter

indicators.note: the boy takes hold of D, so D sits inside him

explanation.surface: An unruly lad snatches hold of a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grabs' reads as a physical snatch in the surface; in the wordplay it just means the boy's name holds the letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wildly is acting without any restraint.

clue.text: Hard to make out behind replica designed by European

indicators.note: the letters are designed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: E = European, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A copy of an artwork, reworked by someone from the Continent, is barely legible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word, but it is fodder, letters to be rearranged along with REPLICA and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indecipherable cannot be read or understood: it is hard to make out.

clue.text: Create film music from scratch

blocks.note: what a composer does for a soundtrack, a verb
a verb too: cut a line into a surface, as with a knife on card

explanation.surface: A composer writes a soundtrack starting with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From scratch' reads as one idiom, meaning with nothing prepared; split it and 'scratch' is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: writing the music that accompanies a film, and marking a surface with a cut line.

clue.text: Specialist used it with chancel refurbishment

indicators.note: refurbishing reworks the letters into a new form

explanation.surface: An expert brought in to restore the chancel, the part of a church around the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: The chancel is the area of a church around the altar; the surface reads as a church restoration job.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical and specialist both describe knowledge belonging to an expert field.

clue.text: Grease spilt over cheese cloth

indicators.note: something spilt is tipped over, so the word turns round

blocks.note: fat = grease; it turns round to TAF

explanation.surface: Cooking fat splashed across a cheesecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese cloth' looks like one kitchen item; it splits into the cheese (FETA) and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven silk cloth.

clue.text: By and large this garment's unfinished

indicators.note: the word stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: the one-piece work suit pulled on over clothes; 'unfinished' drops its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that, broadly speaking, the piece of clothing isn't done.
explanation.walkthrough: The garment is a pair of overalls; cut off the final S and you have OVERALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall means taken as a whole, which is what 'by and large' means.

clue.text: Be passionate about teacher's initial suggestion for sacrifice

indicators.note: the initial letter of 'teacher' is the one taken

blocks.note: to burn for something is to be passionate about it
an offering is something put forward, a suggestion

explanation.surface: A keen teacher proposes giving something up, perhaps for Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: The T in BURNT comes from the teacher, not from the verb; BURN and T just happen to spell the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Bible: an animal or gift burnt whole on an altar to God.

clue.text: Tape of call capturing point at which company doctor returned

indicators.note: the doctor comes back, so DR turns round to RD
RING holds the other letters inside it

blocks.note: to ring is to call on the phone
Dr = doctor; it turns round to RD

explanation.surface: A recording of a phone call captures the moment a firm's medic came back.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the doctor is 'returned'; the point and the company go in as written. 'Point' is a compass point, a common crossword source of N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun 'tape' stands by extension for whatever was captured on the magnetic tape, e.g. an interview.

clue.text: Fresh direction with actors producing programme

blocks.note: the actors in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: A new director teams up with a troupe of actors to make a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' pretends to be a director's work, but it is just a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a bulletin of the day's news is one kind of broadcast programme.

clue.text: Dairy product church head decrees is off

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The head of the church declares the milk has gone sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church head' reads as a bishop or pope, but 'church' alone gives CH and 'head' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the hard yellow cheese from Somerset is one of many foods made from milk.

clue.text: Distribute loot due by arrangement

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Thieves share out the takings owed to each, as agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a gang divvying up its haul, which is exactly what doling out means.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: handing something out in measured portions, like rations or charity.

clue.text: Fruit grew to be fashionable

explanation.surface: A fruit that became trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSE is the past tense of rise, so it means grew in the sense of increased.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the red seed pod a rose bush forms after flowering is botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Skip start of funny visual

indicators.note: the first letter is skipped over

blocks.note: jocular = joking, funny; its first letter J is skipped

explanation.surface: Advice to leave out the opening of a comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skip' looks like a verb about jumping; here it tells you to drop the J of JOCULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eyes, so visual.

clue.text: Wary of motoring organisation backing fuel modification

indicators.note: going backwards turns RAC round to CAR
the letters of FUEL are modified into a new order

blocks.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation; it turns round to CAR

explanation.surface: Suspicious of a motoring club that supports changes to petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British breakdown and motoring organisation. 'Backing' pretends to mean supporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful and wary both mean cautious, alert to danger.

clue.text: Lead singer rehearses The Sound of Music

indicators.note: the leading letter of 'singer' is the one taken

explanation.surface: The star vocalist runs through the musical The Sound of Music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead singer' is a band's frontman in the surface; here 'Lead' takes only the S. The definition is the musical's title read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Strains are snatches of melody, literally the sound of music.

clue.text: Less occupied with identity, Lear loses Cordelia, finally

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so Lear's name goes on without that letter
the final letter of 'Cordelia' is the one meant

blocks.note: the king's name as it stands, before the loss
last letter of Cordelia, the letter Lear loses

explanation.surface: King Lear, stripped of his identity, loses his daughter Cordelia at the end of the play.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Cordelia dies at the end, which the surface leans on; the wordplay only wants her last letter, A.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the comparative: 'idle' means unoccupied, so its -er form means less busy.

clue.text: Hippy gear?

blocks.note: the surface wants a sixties flower child; the setter means 'of the hips'
clothing, so a garment worn round the hips and little else

explanation.surface: A question about what hippies wear: beads, kaftans and flares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hippy' pretends to mean flower-power; read it as 'of the hips', and the gear is clothing worn round the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single piece of cloth wrapped round the hips.

clue.text: Send back a large piece of lightweight material

indicators.note: sending the letters back turns them round

blocks.note: a slab is a large piece

explanation.surface: Returning a big chunk of flimsy fabric to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A SLAB reads backwards as BALSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood used in model-making.

clue.text: Is it the fashion to get very cross?

blocks.note: the current craze, as in the idiom 'all the ___'
a verb: to fume, storm, lose your temper

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether losing your temper is now trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the rage' means in fashion, so 'the rage' is the fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The rage is the current craze; to rage is to be furious.

clue.text: Design of poster etc is hush-hush

indicators.note: the letters are designed into a new pattern

explanation.surface: The artwork for a campaign is being kept under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Etc' is fodder too, which is rare: its three letters supply the C, E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush-hush and top secret both mean kept strictly confidential.
